observations.text: Re-review delta at commit f69fcdd. The supports compile into every review-app target, so the whole package was built and run. I observed the RED myself with a resume-only mutation. Mutation: in crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/resume.rs, PlanRowStatus::Read => resume.already_read.push(position) became PlanRowStatus::Read => {}, so the verdict drops every row the scan already read; the new fault, the adapter and the app were untouched. ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume; exit 101; 5 passed, 6 failed in 6.02 s. The new journey a_run_cut_short_after_saving_a_read_of_its_own_keeps_it_for_the_run_after_it fails at left 1, right 2 - her queue accounting only for the one repo the run that finished read, where her scan read two - exactly the loss E2 names, beside L1/F101 (left {} right {0, 2}) and the four other journeys (left 2 right 3, left 1 right 3, left 2 right 3, left 2 right 3). Restored by the run's own trap with git checkout --; no proptest regression file was written or remains; git status --porcelain empty; ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume; exit 0; 11 passed in 6.09 s.

The new journey observes E2 at the public port and adds two observations no other test made. With the after-first fault held, her scan of two repos saves its first read, is refused the second and ends interrupted; the journey asserts that her queue accounts for NO repos read while that run is unfinished, which is the design's own constraint that a count belongs to a completed run and was until now only stated; then, with the fault lifted, the run she picks up reads only the repo still owed, and the journey asserts that this run read fewer repos than the whole scan and not none, so a count of two cannot be produced by the last run alone - the discriminator the earlier cut-short journey could not supply, since there the interrupted run had saved nothing of its own. It reuses when_scans, when_she_picks_the_run_up, when_her_store_saves_reads_again, repos_read_lines, then_the_run_ended and the shared count assertion rather than adding a parallel one, and the generalised then_her_scan_read_the_repos_she_chose now takes the chosen repos as an argument, so the two-repo and three-repo journeys share one WHAT/WHY/HOW message that still names the chosen set.

Closure after this delta: eleven executable observations in the suite plus the architectural check and three adapter-level tests bind P1 and P2 and every declared obligation. L6's three cases are all bound and all observed - F313 and F314 by the two new adapter tests, and F315 (with no fault held, one run marks two rows read and both are accepted) by reuse of the one-pause journey, whose acceptance text now states that her store saves both of those reads, rather than by a duplicate test. T2 is bound to cargo xtask check-arch and backed by the two new guard cases that fail an ungated fault name and pass a gated one, so the seam this oracle now depends on cannot reach a release build. Timing: 6.03 s, 6.02 s and 6.09 s wall for 11 tests of which six drive the real binary over HTTP, and 4.50 s inside the package run, the share ADR-091 accepts for this family and far below the 300 s ceiling; nothing sits near half of its own budget, so no nine-run median evidence was collected. typesafe: unavailable, carried from the probe recorded this session (TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent from this process environment); every judgment here is locally derived from the measured runs and the read bytes.

diagnostic: Accepted, with no finding open. E2 is now observed instead of excused: with the declared after-first fault held, her scan of two repos saves its first read, is refused the second and ends interrupted; her queue accounts for no repos read while it is unfinished; and once her store saves again, the run she picks up reads only the repo still owed and her queue says two repos read although that run read one. The journey adds two observations nothing else made - that an unfinished run carries no count, and that the run which finished read strictly fewer repos than the scan, so a count of two cannot come from the last run alone - which is the discriminator the earlier cut-short journey lacked, its interrupted run having saved nothing of its own. I observed the RED myself with a resume-only mutation that drops the rows the scan already read: the new journey fails at left 1, right 2, beside L1/F101 and the four other journeys, and after restoring the file the suite is green again at 11 passed, with the tree clean and no regression file. Because the two supports compile into every review-app target, the whole package was built and run: 22 targets, 322 passed, 0 failed; the adapter and xtask suites pass with the two L6 tests and the two new fault-name guard cases named in their output, and cargo xtask check-arch, T2's own check, exits 0, so the seam this oracle now depends on cannot reach a release build. L6's three cases are all bound, F315 by reuse of the one-pause journey rather than a duplicate. No design, implementation or product finding; nothing in this delta blocks completion.
